rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), through Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/02 dated February 3, 2026, is seeking comments and feedback on a proposed shift to an XBRL-based filing framework for Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) applications. The proposal would replace the current application-based process, under which listed entities manually enter information and upload supporting documents in PDF format, with an XBRL-exclusive filing process.

The document explains that listed entities are already required under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015, SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, and other applicable provisions/circulars/guidance notes, to obtain Stock Exchange approval for QIP-related issuances. The approvals covered in this proposal are the in-principle approval and post-allotment listing approval (the circular text also refers generally to QIP applications and notes that companies currently file in-principle approval, post-allotment approval, and trading approval requests with the exchange). The stated rationale is to continue the exchanges’ phased migration from document-based filings to XBRL reporting in order to standardize securities market data, improve regulatory efficiency, and make filing and monitoring easier for both listed entities and the exchange.

If implemented as described, the new requirement would mean that QIP-related information must be filed by listed entities in XBRL only, using the prescribed XBRL formats that the circular says are being made available. The document is framed as a consultation/feedback exercise rather than an effective rule change, so it does not itself set a compliance deadline or effective date for mandatory adoption; instead, it asks stakeholders to review and comment on the proposed transition.

rows.summary:
The NSE has issued an update to its single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges, referring back to its circular of September 30, 2024. The main change is that the single filing system has now been extended to cover **Integrated Filing (Financials)** under **Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, and this extension is **effective January 03, 2026**. This means listed entities that fall within the applicable categories can use the API-based single filing mechanism for this financial disclosure instead of separate filings, subject to the availability and applicability set out by the exchange.

The circular identifies the disclosures currently available through the single filing system and ties each one to its governing regulation and rollout date. For **Integrated Filing (Financials)**, the relevant provisions are **Regulation 23(9), Regulation 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, Regulation 32(1), and Regulation 33(3)**, and the facility is marked as available from **January 03, 2026** for **equity** and **equity+debt** listed companies; for **exclusively debt** issuers and **REITs/INVITs**, the circular says the position will be **communicated later**. The other disclosures already listed as part of the broader single filing framework are **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** effective **September 15, 2025**; **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** effective **March 01, 2025**; **Meetings of shareholders and voting results** under **Regulation 44(3)** effective **December 28, 2024**; and **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** effective **November 15, 2024**.

The circular also clarifies a status change for the **Corporate Governance Report** under **Regulation 27(2)**: it was effective **October 26, 2024**, but has now been **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to a **SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**. For the categories where the table shows “shall be communicated later,” the exchange has not yet provided implementation timing for **exclusively debt** and **REIT/INVIT** entities for some filings, so compliance teams for those entity types should not assume immediate availability beyond what is expressly stated. In practical terms, listed entities should verify whether they are in the **equity** or **equity+debt** category to determine immediate use of the API-based single filing system for financials from **January 3, 2026**, and they should continue following the prescribed SEBI regulation-specific filing obligations through the single filing mechanism as rolled out by the exchange.

rows.summary:
SEBI has issued Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/135 dated October 13, 2025**, which is being circulated by NSE to all listed entities. The circular does **not create an entirely new RPT approval framework**, but reinforces that listed entities must follow the **“Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions”** standards already formulated by the **Industry Standards Forum (ISF)** under the SEBI Master Circular dated **November 11, 2024** and SEBI Circular dated **June 26, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that **minimum disclosure information for Related Party Transaction (RPT) approvals must be provided to both the Audit Committee and shareholders** when seeking approval for such transactions. This applies to **all listed entities** and is relevant whenever an RPT requires approval at either forum. The document is a direction to follow the ISF-issued standards, meaning companies should ensure their board/audit committee/shareholder approval materials contain the required minimum information set out under those standards, rather than relying on ad hoc or incomplete transaction summaries.

The NSE circular dated **October 14, 2025** simply forwards SEBI’s October 13 circular and states that it is for the recipient’s **reference and necessary action**. No separate numeric threshold, filing deadline, or monetary limit is stated in the excerpt provided; however, the compliance obligation is immediate in the sense that listed entities are expected to align their RPT approval materials with the prescribed minimum information requirements already in force under the SEBI framework. Compliance teams should therefore review current RPT approval templates, audit committee notes, and shareholder resolution support documents to ensure they conform to the ISF minimum-information standard before the next RPT approval cycle.

rows.title: Filing of Financial Results by REITs & InvITs in XBRL Mode
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/38 Date: October 09, 2025 To, All Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) All Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) Subject: Filing of Financial Results by REITs & InvITs in XBRL Mode This is in reference to the SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 dated July 11, 2025, for REITs & SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 dated July 11, 2025, for InvITs, regarding Chapter 4 - Continuous Disclosures and Compliances by REITs & InvITs wherein the format for submission of financial results by REITs & InvITs has been revised as per the aforesaid Master circulars. In this regard, we wish to inform you that the excel utility for submission of Financial Results-REITs & InvITs as per the revised format has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results The REITs & InvITs are required to submit the financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the financial results in PDF mode using the excel utility “Financial Results_Invits_Reits” In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, you may contact the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to listingfr@nse.co.in Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Mandar Walavalkar Vice President-Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has issued a listing compliance circular dated October 9, 2025 to all REITs and all InvITs requiring them to file financial results in XBRL mode using a revised format. The change is based on SEBI’s Master Circulars dated July 11, 2025 — SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 for REITs and SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 for InvITs — which revised the financial results submission format under Chapter 4 on continuous disclosures and compliances.

NSE states that the updated Excel utility for the revised format is now available on the NEAPS portal at Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results, and the file name to use is “Financial Results_Invits_Reits.” The compliance obligation is that REITs and InvITs must submit their financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours after submitting the financial results in PDF mode. In practical terms, this creates a two-step filing process: first the PDF submission, then the XBRL submission within the 24-hour window.

For operational questions, the circular directs entities to the contact details available on NEAPS under NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance, or to email listingfr@nse.co.in. No separate effective date beyond the circular date is stated, so the requirement appears to apply immediately upon issuance and use of the revised filing utility.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated its single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges, expanding it to include the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report under Regulation 24A(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, with **effect from September 15, 2025**. This means listed entities covered by this reporting obligation will be able to submit the report through the single-filing/API mechanism instead of separate exchange filings, in line with the NSE’s earlier circular dated September 30, 2024 on the same system.

The circular also restates the set of disclosures currently covered by the API-based single filing framework and their implementation dates: **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** became effective **October 1, 2024** and is noted as being **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024; **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** became effective **October 26, 2024**; **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** became effective **November 15, 2024**; **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results under Regulation 44(3)** became effective **December 28, 2024**; and **Integrated Filing (Governance) under Regulations 13(3), 27(2) and 30** became effective **March 1, 2025**. The newly added **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report under Regulation 24A(2)** is effective **September 15, 2025**.

For applicability, the circular indicates the single-filing/API system is available to **equity-listed companies** and **equity + debt listed companies** for the covered disclosures marked with a tick in the table. The table also indicates that for **exclusively debt listed entities** and for **REITs and InvITs**, availability for some items is marked **“shall be communicated later,”** meaning the NSE has not yet announced implementation for those categories. The practical compliance requirement is that affected listed entities should route the applicable reports through the single filing system via API-based integration starting on the stated effective dates, so that filings are captured once and shared across exchanges under the framework.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/36 dated September 4, 2025) informs all listed entities that SEBI’s June 26, 2025 circular on the “Industry Standards on Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)” is now accompanied by FAQs for implementation guidance and necessary action. The most important compliance point is that the RPT Industry Standards **replace the prior RPT disclosure formats** in Section III-B of NSE’s Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, rather than merely supplement them. The FAQ expressly states that the new standards substitute the Section III-B disclosure requirement from the “specified date,” and if any part of the standards conflicts with later amendments to the LODR Regulations and/or SEBI circulars, those later regulatory changes prevail.

For compliance teams, the practical impact is that listed entities must use the new minimum-information framework when preparing materials for **Audit Committee review** and **Shareholder approval** of related party transactions, instead of the old disclosure templates under the Master Circular. The document does not introduce a separate numerical threshold, rate, or transaction cap; its significance is in changing the **required disclosure format/content** for RPT approval processes and clarifying that the FAQs should be used as reference and for necessary action. The circular also points readers to NSE’s website for the circular text and the enclosed FAQs, which should be treated as part of the implementation guidance for determining what information must be provided in RPT approval submissions.

rows.title: Processing of waiver applications by the Exchanges in case of commonly listed entities.
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/35 Date: August 26, 2025 To All Listed Entities, Subject: Processing of waiver applications by the Exchanges in case of commonly listed entities SEBI vide SOP Circular ref. no. SEBI vide Master circular dated November 11, 2024 (ref no. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/0155) (Erstwhile Circular ref no. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD/CIR/P/2020/12 dated January 22, 2020) directed the Exchanges to put in place a framework to monitor submissions made by listed entities and to initiate actions such as levy of penalties, moving of security to ‘Z’ category, freezing of promoter holdings and suspension of trading in securities of non-compliant listed entities. Further, SEBI in its above-mentioned Circulars directed the Exchanges that they may deviate from the actions prescribed in SOP Circulars, if found necessary, only after recording reasons in writing. In view of the above, the Exchanges constituted Internal Committees for reviewing the requests received for waiver of SOP fines based on the extant norms. In order to achieve the objectives of streamlining the process of disposal of waiver requests, expediting the disposals and maintaining uniformity of actions/decisions involving commonly listed Companies, the Exchanges in consultation with SEBI have agreed that waiver applications received from commonly listed entities shall be segregated so that only one of the Exchanges will process the application and the decision shall be binding on all other Exchanges which have levied penalties on the Companies for the same non- compliance. It has also been agreed that a nominal non-refundable processing fee shall be charged by the Exchange tasked with the disposal of the waiver application. The details of the procedural aspects of the said policy including the applicable processing fees, which shall be effective for applications seeking waiver of SOP fines submitted to the exchanges on or after September 01, 2025 i
rows.summary:
NSE has announced a new procedure for waiver applications relating to SOP fines for **commonly listed entities**—that is, listed companies that are listed on more than one exchange. The change is intended to streamline handling of waiver requests, speed up disposal, and ensure uniform outcomes where the same non-compliance has resulted in penalties from multiple exchanges. Under the new arrangement, waiver applications from such entities will be **segregated so that only one exchange processes the request**, and the **decision of that one exchange will be binding on all other exchanges** that have levied penalties for the same non-compliance.

This policy is being implemented in the context of SEBI’s SOP framework, under which exchanges monitor listed-entity filings and may impose actions such as **penalties, shifting securities to the “Z” category, freezing promoter holdings, and suspension of trading** for non-compliance. SEBI has also required that if an exchange deviates from the prescribed SOP actions, it must do so **only after recording written reasons**. To handle waiver requests, exchanges had already constituted internal committees, and this circular formalizes a coordinated process for commonly listed companies.

A further new requirement is that the exchange assigned to process the waiver application will charge a **nominal non-refundable processing fee**. The circular states that the detailed procedural aspects and the applicable fee schedule are provided in the policy, and that these rules will apply to **waiver applications seeking waiver of SOP fines submitted on or after September 1, 2025**.

For compliance purposes, this means any commonly listed entity seeking waiver of SOP fines after that effective date should expect the application to be handled through a single designated exchange rather than separately across multiple exchanges, and the resulting decision will apply across all exchanges involved in the same penalty matter. Companies should also budget for the new **non-refundable processing fee** and ensure waiver submissions are complete and timely under the new single-processing framework.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular is an intimation to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), all parties to InvITs, and all registered depositories that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/114 dated August 8, 2025, titled **“Review of Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT.”** The NSE notice itself does not set out the operative regulatory changes, conditions, thresholds, or procedural steps; it simply forwards SEBI’s circular and states that the enclosed SEBI circular should be referred to for “necessary action.”  

From a compliance perspective, the immediate requirement is to review the SEBI circular enclosed with the NSE communication and assess whether the entity is a **private listed InvIT** seeking conversion to a **public InvIT**, or is otherwise involved in that conversion process as a party or depository. The date of the NSE notice is **August 12, 2025**, and it refers to the SEBI circular issued **August 8, 2025**; no separate compliance deadline is stated in the NSE text itself. The NSE notice also indicates the circular is available on the NSE website for reference.  

Because the NSE communication is purely forwarding information, it does **not** specify any new obligations, filing forms, approvals, eligibility criteria, timelines, percentage thresholds, valuation requirements, or investor-protection conditions on its face. A compliance team should therefore treat this as a trigger to obtain and analyze the underlying SEBI circular, which is the document that contains the actual framework for conversion and any actionable requirements.

(‘SEBI LODR’) With reference to: A. SEBI circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/59 dated April 29, 2025, regarding “Clarificatory and Procedural changes to aid and strengthen ESG Rating Providers (ERPs)”, which stated: 1.3. Disclosure of Rating Rationale on the website of Stock Exchange(s): 1.3.1. For ESG ratings of an issuer/ entity, the stock exchange where such issuer is listed shall prominently disclose the ESG rating on its website under a separate tab/ section on the listed company’s page 1.3.2. For ESG ratings of a debt security, the stock exchange where the security is listed shall prominently disclose the ESG rating on its website under a separate tab/ section on the listed security’s page Considering the aforementioned circulars, the Exchanges, in consulta
rows.summary:
This circular sets out the stock-exchange-led, system-driven disclosure framework for two types of ratings under SEBI LODR: credit ratings reported under Regulation 30(6) read with sub-para 3 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III, and ESG ratings disclosed under the ESG Rating Provider framework. It is issued to all listed entities, all SEBI-registered credit rating agencies (CRAs), and all SEBI-registered ESG rating providers (ERPs), and it follows earlier SEBI directions that exchanges, in consultation with SEBI, must define the process, procedure, and timelines for automated disclosure of “new rating(s) or revision in ratings,” as well as publication of ESG ratings on stock-exchange websites.

For credit ratings, the circular implements system-driven disclosure for any new rating or revision in rating that is required to be filed/disclosed by a listed entity under Regulation 30(6). The practical effect is that the disclosure will be generated through the exchange system rather than relying only on manual issuer-driven publication. Listed entities remain responsible for the underlying compliance event, but the exchange infrastructure becomes the mechanism for public dissemination of the rating information once the rating is filed.

For ESG ratings, the circular gives effect to SEBI’s April 29, 2025 clarificatory/procedural changes requiring stock exchanges to prominently display ESG ratings on their websites in a separate tab/section. If the ESG rating is for an issuer/entity, the disclosure must appear on the stock exchange where that issuer is listed, on the listed company’s page; if the ESG rating is for a debt security, the disclosure must appear on the stock exchange where that security is listed, on the listed security’s page. The requirement is specifically for prominent website disclosure in a dedicated section, not buried in a generic filings area.

The circular is operative as part of the exchanges’ implementation of the SEBI framework referenced above, so compliance teams should assume these disclosures will be system-triggered through exchange infrastructure and should ensure ratings data submitted to CRAs/ERPs and exchanged via the listed entity’s filing processes is accurate, timely, and complete. From a controls perspective, listed entities should verify that rating actions they are required to disclose under LODR are promptly captured in the exchange system, and they should confirm that the relevant stock exchange page reflects the correct credit rating and ESG rating information for the issuer or debt security as applicable.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated July 31, 2025, introduces a **Joint Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for applications filed under **Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** in relation to **schemes of arrangement**. It is stated to be **in addition to** NSE Circular **NSE/CML/2023/70 dated September 29, 2023** and BSE Notice **20230929-30 dated September 29, 2023**, and it was issued because SEBI advised the exchanges to streamline and expedite the scheme-of-arrangement approval process.

The circular applies to **all listed entities** and their **company secretaries** that are proposing or are involved in a scheme of arrangement. It specifies that the SOP and related guidance are to be read with the **SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 and May 21, 2024**. The document lists several supporting materials: an SOP for applications under Reg. 37 and Reg. 59A, an SOP for applications seeking relaxation under **sub-rule (7) of rule 19 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957**, checklists for both types of applications, and FAQs on schemes of arrangement.

The key effective date is explicit: **the circular is applicable with effect from August 1, 2025**. From that date onward, listed entities filing a draft scheme of arrangement before any court or tribunal must follow the new joint SOP and the associated checklist/FAQ framework for their regulatory submissions. The document excerpt provided begins the Annexure I SOP by stating that a listed entity desirous of undertaking or involved in a scheme of arrangement must file the **draft scheme of arrangement** before the relevant judicial forum under the applicable legal provisions, indicating that the filing process is being standardized at the exchange level for Reg. 37 and 59A matters.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued Listing Circular NSE/CML/2025/31 on July 23, 2025 to all listed entities, through their company secretaries, regarding dividend payments to parties whose bank accounts are attached under the Special Court (TORTS) Act, 1992. The Exchange says it received a letter from the Custodian’s office and is directing listed entities to ensure that whenever an online dividend payment is credited into the bank account of any notified party, the listed entity must send intimation of that credit to the Custodian’s office without fail for further necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the practical requirement is not a change in dividend policy or a new payment threshold, but a mandatory notification step tied to dividend credits made into attached accounts of notified parties under the Special Court (TORTS) Act regime. The circular does not specify a separate deadline date, implementation window, monetary threshold, or reporting format; instead, it requires immediate and consistent compliance whenever such a credit occurs. Listed entities should therefore have procedures in place to identify when dividend disbursements are made to notified parties subject to account attachment and to ensure prompt communication to the Custodian each time. The circular closes by stating that listed entities are “once again requested” to take note and comply accordingly, indicating the Exchange expects ongoing adherence rather than a one-time action.

NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2025/30 dated July 7, 2025 expands the Exchange’s XBRL filing framework to cover Regulation 30 disclosures for the award, bagging/receipt, amendment, or termination of orders/contracts, whether entered into in the ordinary course of business or otherwise. For compliance purposes, NSE states that at the initial stage it will treat the **PDF filing** as satisfying the listed entity’s Regulation 30 disclosure obligation, but the entity must then file the same disclosure in **XBRL within 24 hours** of submitting the PDF. The Exchange also notes that the XBRL disclosure will be made available in **iXBRL** format on NSE’s corporate filings/announcements webpage and in NEAPS under **Report >> Announcement XBRL Report**, so companies should expect the submission to flow into both the public website and internal reporting views.

The circular also reinforces that disclosures about awarding/bagging of orders/contracts should not be routed merely as **Updates** or **Press Release** items; they should be filed through the prescribed Regulation 30 announcement process. In practical terms, listed entities need to ensure their internal workflows identify these contract/order events, prepare the PDF disclosure promptly, and then complete the XBRL upload within the 24-hour window to remain compliant with the Exchange’s filing process.

Regulation 23(2), (3) and (4) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulations”) require related party transactions (“RPTs”) to be approved by the audit committee and by the shareho
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued a circular dated **June 26, 2025** establishing **industry standards on the minimum information that must be provided to the Audit Committee and to shareholders when seeking approval for Related Party Transactions (RPTs)** under **Regulations 23(2), 23(3) and 23(4) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The circular applies to **all listed entities** and is also addressed to the **recognized stock exchanges** and industry bodies; the NSE has circulated it to listed entities for implementation. The practical compliance change is that companies can no longer rely on generic or minimal RPT papers: they must now provide the **prescribed minimum set of information, in the specified format**, to support approval by the Audit Committee and, where required, shareholders.

The circular is part of SEBI’s effort to standardize RPT approval materials across the market, so that the decision-makers receive consistent information before approving a transaction. For compliance teams, the key implication is that **all RPT proposals placed before the Audit Committee and shareholders must be prepared in line with the new industry standards note enclosed with the circular**, and those materials should contain the minimum disclosures required by the standard before approval is sought. The document also indicates that SEBI expects listed entities to take **“necessary action”** based on the circular and accompanying standards note, meaning internal RPT approval templates, board/audit committee packs, and shareholder approval documentation may need to be revised immediately.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - Extension of automated implementation of trading window closure to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons, on account of declaration of financial results
rows.desc: Circular Department: Investigation Download Ref No: NSE/CML/22 Date: April 21, 2025 To All Listed Companies, Sub: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - Extension of automated implementation of trading window closure to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons, on account of declaration of financial results This has reference to NSE Circular no. NSE/CML/2024/08 dated March 28, 2024, NSE Circular no. NSE/CML/2024/03 dated January 30, 2024, NSE/CML/2023/79 dated November 17, 2023, NSE/CML/2022/40 dated August 05, 2022, NSE/CML/2023/49 dated June 28, 2023 and NSE/CML/2023/59 dated July 31, 2023 and in accordance with Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) circular no. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-SEC-4/P/CIR/2022/107 dated August 5, 2022 and SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD- 2/P/CIR/2023/124 dated July 19, 2023, regarding Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD- 2/P/CIR/2025/55 dated April 21, 2025, regarding Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) Extension of automated implementation of trading window closure to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons, on account of declaration of financial results. In order to ease the compliance with Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of PIT Regulations and to prevent inadvertent non-compliances of provisions of PIT Regulations by designated persons (“DPs”), as mandated by SEBI Master Circular on Surveillance of Securities Market dated Sep
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated April 21, 2025 informs all listed companies of SEBI’s new circular dated the same day, which extends the automated trading window closure mechanism to the immediate relatives of designated persons (“DPs”) when financial results are being declared. This is an expansion of the earlier framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it builds on prior NSE circulars from 2022–2024 that implemented the system of freezing PAN at the security level to restrict trading by DPs during closed periods.

The key change is that, where a company has to close the trading window on account of declaration of financial results, the automated restriction is no longer limited to the DP alone; it now also applies to the DP’s immediate relatives. The purpose, as stated by SEBI, is to make compliance easier and to reduce inadvertent violations of the PIT Regulations by DPs and persons connected to them. The circular does not create a new trading restriction period or alter the underlying obligation to keep the trading window closed; rather, it broadens the population subject to the existing automated block.

For compliance teams, the practical requirement is to ensure that systems and records used for PAN-based trading restrictions at the security level are capable of identifying and freezing trading access for immediate relatives of DPs during the trading window closure period triggered by financial results. Companies should verify that their internal insider lists, relative mappings, and automated controls are updated so the restriction is implemented correctly and consistently. The circular is issued in continuation of the earlier NSE/SEBI circulars referenced in it and should be treated as an operational enhancement to existing PIT compliance procedures rather than a standalone regime.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/20 Date: April 02, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Updates on the Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities- Disclosure of Integrated Filing- Financial This has reference to the SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’) and read with Exchange’s circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 dated January 02, 2025, regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities. In this connection, this is to inform you that the XBRL utility for Integrated Filing - Financial has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial Listed entities are required to submit financial results in XBRL mode using “Integrated Filing-Financial” utility only. Note: 1. Outcome of the Board Meeting in PDF mode for Financial Results to be submitted within the prescribed timelines of 30 mins or 3 hours as may be applicable, on the below path only: Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/ corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results 2. Further, the listed entities shall submit Integrated Filing - Financial in XBRL on same date of submission of the financial results (in PDF form), on the below path only: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing - Financial Please note that the following shall be discontinued w.e.f. April 01, 2025: 1. Financial results submitted in PDF form under NEAPS - Quick Results tab 2. PDF filing of ‘Integrated Filing - Financial’ in the Corporate Announcement under following path: NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/C
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated listed entities on the rollout of the SEBI-mandated “Integrated Filing - Financial” process under SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024, as referenced in the Exchange’s earlier circular dated January 2, 2025. The key operational change is that the XBRL utility for “Integrated Filing - Financial” is now available on the NEAPS portal, and listed entities must use this utility only to submit financial results in XBRL mode via the path Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial. In parallel, the outcome of the Board Meeting for financial results must still be filed in PDF format within the applicable prescribed timeline of 30 minutes or 3 hours, as relevant, but only through the announcement path specified in the circular: Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results.

A further obligation is that the Integrated Filing - Financial submission in XBRL must be made on the same date as the PDF filing of the financial results. The circular also makes clear that certain older filing methods have been discontinued effective April 1, 2025: financial results can no longer be submitted in PDF form through the NEAPS “Quick Results” tab, and the PDF filing of “Integrated Filing - Financial” through the Corporate Announcement route is also discontinued. This update applies to all listed entities on the NSE and specifically governs how they must file financial results and related board-meeting outcomes going forward.

SEBI Circular Page 1 of 4 CIRCULAR SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 March 28, 2025 To, All listed entities All the recognized Stock Exchanges Dear Sir/Madam, Sub: Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. 1. Based on the recommendations of the Expert Committee for Facilitating Ease of Doing Business and pursuant to public consultation, the Board, on December 18, 2024, decided to revise various provisions regarding ESG disclosures for value chain, provide an option to undertake ‘assessment’ or ‘assurance’ for BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduce disclosure on green credits. 2. Accordingly, the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulation
rows.summary:
SEBI has amended the sustainability/ESG compliance framework for listed entities to make it easier to implement, mainly by revising the rules on BRSR Core assurance/assessment, changing the treatment of ESG disclosures for the value chain, and creating a new voluntary disclosure regime for green credits. The change follows recommendations of SEBI’s Expert Committee for Facilitating Ease of Doing Business and a public consultation, and SEBI states that its Board approved these revisions on December 18, 2024; the operative circular is SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 dated March 28, 2025, with the NSE circular issued April 1, 2025 for dissemination to all listed entities.

For compliance purposes, the key substantive change is that listed entities now have an option to obtain either “assessment” or “assurance” in relation to BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for the value chain, rather than being limited to only one approach. The circular also revises the disclosure framework for ESG matters in the value chain, meaning entities that make or plan to make those disclosures need to follow the updated SEBI requirements and any associated methodology/verification expectations set out in the amended LODR framework. In addition, SEBI has introduced a voluntary disclosure on green credits, so entities may disclose information about green credits if they choose, but this is not framed as mandatory for all listed entities.

The circular is addressed to all listed entities and recognized stock exchanges, so the immediate practical effect is on listed companies that are subject to SEBI LODR compliance, especially those preparing BRSR Core disclosures, value-chain ESG disclosures, or considering voluntary sustainability reporting around green credits. Because the NSE notice says the SEBI circular is enclosed “for reference and necessary action,” compliance teams should treat this as an implementation update requiring review of current ESG reporting controls, assurance/assessment arrangements, and disclosure templates to align with the revised regime. The document excerpt provided does not include specific filing deadlines, numeric thresholds, or rate changes, so those details would need to be confirmed from the full enclosed SEBI circular if applicable to the entity’s reporting cycle.

No.: NSE/CML/2025/07 dated February 28, 2025 regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities in relation to the filing of Integrated Filing-Governance. In this connection, this is to inform you that: 1. The timeline for submission of XBRL for Integrated Filing-Governance from the quarter ended March 31, 2025 onwards, is 30 days from the end of quarter. 2. The listed entities shall submit only Integrated Filing-Governance (XBRL form) within 30 days from the end of the quarter. 3. From quarter ended March 31, 2025 onwards, the listed entities are not required to submit the existing XBRL of Corporate Governance and Investor Grievance Report as per the current process. In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to takeover@nse.co.in/nsexbrl@nse.co.in. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head -Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has revised the filing requirement for listed entities’ governance-related reporting under the Integrated Filing-Governance framework, effective for the quarter ended March 31, 2025 onward. Beginning with that quarter, the XBRL submission for Integrated Filing-Governance must be filed within **30 days from the end of the quarter**. Listed entities are required to submit **only the Integrated Filing-Governance XBRL form** in that timeframe, and the previous separate XBRL filings for **Corporate Governance** and the **Investor Grievance Report** are no longer required under the current process.

This update is issued by NSE Listing Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2025/16** dated **April 01, 2025**, and it references the underlying SEBI circular dated **December 31, 2024** as well as prior NSE implementation circulars dated **January 02, 2025**, **January 13, 2025**, and **February 28, 2025**. The practical compliance change is a consolidation of governance reporting into one XBRL filing with a clear 30-day post-quarter deadline, replacing the earlier dual-reporting process. For queries, entities are directed to the NEAPS platform under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or to email **takeover@nse.co.in** / **nsexbrl@nse.co.in**.

rows.summary:
This update postpones the effective date of SEBI’s Industry Standards on the “Minimum information to be provided for review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for approval of a related party transaction” from **April 1, 2025 to July 1, 2025**. The change comes in response to stakeholder feedback requesting more time to implement the standards. The updated requirement applies to **all listed entities** and concerns the information that must be presented when seeking **Audit Committee and shareholder approval for related party transactions**.

For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is unchanged in substance but the implementation timeline is extended: listed entities must now ensure they are aligned with the Industry Standards by **July 1, 2025** rather than April 1, 2025. The circular references SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/18 dated February 14, 2025**, and confirms that the revised effective date is being issued through SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/37 dated March 21, 2025**. No new thresholds, rates, or numerical limits are introduced in this update; the material change is the **deferral of applicability**.

The National Stock Exchange of India has circulated this SEBI update to all listed entities and notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website. Compliance teams should use the extra time to finalize internal templates, approvals, and disclosure processes for related party transactions so that the revised information package required by the Industry Standards is in place by the new effective date.

The NSE notice identifies the underlying SEBI reference as Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/35, also dated March 20, 2025, and states that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is informational, but it points listed entities to a new SEBI requirement introduced by SEBI circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DCR1/CIR/P/2025/0034 dated March 20, 2025, titled “Online Filing System for reports filed under Regulation 10(7) of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.” The NSE’s notice is addressed to company secretaries of all listed entities and states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for necessary action; it also says the circular is available on the NSE website.

Based on the text provided here, the document does not itself describe the substantive mechanics of the new online filing system, the filing trigger, deadlines, or any thresholds—only that SEBI has issued a circular requiring reports under Regulation 10(7) to be filed through an online system. A compliance team should therefore treat this as a notice that a mandatory filing process has been changed by SEBI effective March 20, 2025, and should review the underlying SEBI circular immediately to determine the exact filing workflow, responsible persons, and any timing or procedural obligations. rows.summary:
The NSE issued a circular on **March 15, 2025** enclosing FAQs on how to apply the **Industry Standards for “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transactions (RPT)”**. The circular is addressed to **all listed entities** and refers back to **NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2025/05 dated February 15, 2025**, which had introduced the underlying industry standards; this new circular does not itself change the substantive standards, but provides interpretive guidance on when the minimum-information requirements apply and asks listed entities to take “necessary action” accordingly.

The FAQs explain that the disclosure/approval framework arises under **Section III-B of the SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024** read with **Regulation 23(2), 23(3) and 23(4) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, which require listed entities to place prescribed information before the **audit committee** and, where required, **shareholders** for consideration of related party transactions. For compliance purposes, the key point is that the industry standards are meant to standardize the **minimum information package** that must be provided for those reviews and approvals; listed entities must therefore align their internal RPT approval materials and processes with the FAQs and the referenced industry standard before sending transactions to the audit committee or shareholders.

The document does not introduce new monetary thresholds, percentage limits, or deadlines beyond the citation date of **March 15, 2025**, but it signals that the FAQs are now part of the compliance reference set for listed entities handling RPT approvals. Companies should ensure that their secretarial, legal, finance, and audit-committee support teams use the FAQ guidance to decide **when** the standards apply, **what minimum information** must be included in board/audit committee/shareholder papers, and that the materials are prepared consistently with the SEBI framework before any required approval is sought.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. Dear Sir / Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/26 dated February 27, 2025, issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (‘SEBI’) titled “Regulatory framework for Specialized Investment Funds (‘SIF’)”. A copy of SEBI Circular dated February 27, 2025, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours Faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Prakash Kelkar Manager- Listing Approval Encl: 1. SEBI Circular Page 1 of 18 CIRCULAR SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/26 February 27, 2025 To, All Mutual Funds All Asset Management Companies (AMCs) All Trustee Companies/ Board of Trustees of Mutual Funds All Registrar and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs) All Recognized Stock Exchanges All Recognized Clearing Corporations All Depositories Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) Madam/ Sir, Subject: Regulatory framework for Specialized Investment Funds (‘SIF’) 1. The landscape of investment management in India has significantly evolved over the years, marked by the introduction and development of various investment products. SEBI has adopted a segmented risk-based approach to regulation of these products depending on their complexity, sophistication of target investors, minimum investment size etc. 2. The current range of investment products with varying risk-reward profiles, are intended to meet the investment needs of retail, high net-worth and institutional investors. The regulatory framework and prudential norms governing these investment vehicles become progressively more flexible from Mutual Funds (‘MFs’)
rows.summary:
This SEBI circular establishes a new regulatory framework for **Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs)** in India and was issued on **February 27, 2025**; the NSE circular forwarding it is dated **March 13, 2025**. It is addressed to **all Mutual Funds, AMCs, trustee companies/boards of trustees, RTAs, recognized stock exchanges, recognized clearing corporations, depositories, and AMFI**, so compliance teams at any of those entities should treat it as potentially applicable. The circular explains that SEBI is expanding its segmented, risk-based approach to investment-product regulation to accommodate a new class of products designed for investors seeking strategies beyond ordinary mutual fund offerings, with prudential norms generally becoming more flexible as products become more sophisticated and targeted toward higher-risk, higher-minimum-investment investors.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this is not merely informational: it introduces a distinct framework for the creation, registration, and operation of **SIFs** under SEBI oversight, and the listed market infrastructure institutions and intermediaries are expected to take “necessary action” to implement it. The circular signals that entities in the mutual fund ecosystem may need to assess whether their existing structures, schemes, or distribution and operational processes can be used for SIFs, and whether any new registration, disclosure, trading, settlement, transfer-agent, depository, or exchange-related procedures will be required under SEBI’s framework. No specific numeric thresholds, fee rates, or hard compliance dates are stated in the excerpt provided, but the operative date of the SEBI circular is **February 27, 2025**, which is the date from which the framework is formally introduced and should be tracked for implementation timing and internal gap assessment.

Because the circular is addressed broadly across the mutual fund value chain, compliance officers should review whether the organization will be affected as an issuer/manager of SIFs, as a trustee/oversight body, or as a service provider supporting operational, listing, settlement, or depository functions for such products. The practical implication is that firms should identify any internal policies, offering documents, investor onboarding standards, disclosures, risk management controls, or systems changes needed to support a product class that sits between traditional mutual funds and other more sophisticated investment vehicles.

Accordingly, the revised timelines for completion of the various activ
rows.summary:
SEBI has introduced a new framework for rights issues through the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, published in the Official Gazette on March 8, 2025, and SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/31 dated March 11, 2025. The key compliance change is that a rights issue must now be completed within **23 working days** from the date the issuer’s Board of Directors approves the rights issue, which materially shortens and standardizes the process timeline under amended Regulation 85 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018.

The circular is addressed to **listed entities, recognized stock exchanges, recognized depositories, registered registrars to an issue and share transfer agents, registered bankers to an issue, self-certified syndicate banks (SCSBs), and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**, so compliance obligations are not limited to issuers alone; market infrastructure participants and intermediaries must also align their procedures to the revised rights issue workflow. The document specifically refers to a **“Faster Rights Issue with a flexibility of allotment to specific investor(s)”**, indicating that the framework permits rights issues to be structured with the ability to allot to identified investors, rather than only through the conventional broad rights entitlement process.

For compliance purposes, the operational point is that all parties involved in a rights issue process must adjust internal controls, sequencing, and service-level timelines to ensure completion within the 23-working-day deadline. The NSE circular dated March 12, 2025, simply forwards SEBI’s circular to “all proposed to be listed entities” and “all the registered Merchant Bankers” for information and necessary action, and notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

rows.summary:
This circular informs listed entities, proposed-to-be-listed entities, recognized stock exchanges, and registered merchant bankers that SEBI has issued a new **Industry Standards Note on disclosures of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in draft offer documents and offer documents**. The purpose is to create a **uniform approach for identifying and disclosing KPIs** in IPO/fund-raising offer documents, so that disclosures are consistent across issuers and reviewed against an industry-standard framework rather than ad hoc company-specific practice.

The circular is dated **February 28, 2025**, and it references **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/28** of the same date. The document states that the SEBI circular and the accompanying Industry Standards Note are enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action, indicating that market participants are expected to align their offer-document disclosure processes with this new standard. The industry standard was developed through the **Industry Standards Forum (ISF)**, comprising **ASSOCHAM, CII, and FICCI**, and is intended to standardize how KPIs are identified and presented in draft offer documents and final offer documents.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway is that **proposed-to-be-listed entities and their merchant bankers must now apply the SEBI-issued industry standard when preparing KPI disclosures in offer documents**. The circular does not itself restate the detailed KPI rules, thresholds, or formulas; instead, it directs recipients to the attached SEBI circular and the Industry Standards Note, which contain the operational requirements that must be followed. No separate effective date, transition period, numeric threshold, or filing deadline is stated in the NSE covering circular itself, but because the reference SEBI circular is dated **February 28, 2025**, compliance teams should treat that date as the governing issuance date and confirm any immediate applicability or implementation timing in the attached SEBI text and industry standards note.

rows.title: Circular on updation of paid up equity capital on a fully diluted basis at Exchange portal
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2025/09 Date: February 28, 2025 To All Members, Sub: U pdation of paid up equity capital on a fully diluted basis at Exchange portal This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. IMD/FPIC/CIR/P/2018/61 dated April 05, 2018 on Monitoring of Foreign Investment Limits in Listed Indian Companies. In this regard, the Listed Companies were required to intimate the Exchange about the paid-up equity capital and paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis (in the term of number of shares) along with the details of conversion ratio (as applicable). However, i t has been observed that Companies have not updated the above data on the NEAPS portal. Therefore, all listed companies are advised to update their paid-up equity capital and paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis (in the term of number of shares) along with the details of conversion ratio (as applicable) on one time basis (even if there are no outstanding convertible instrument) on the NEAPS portal, in case not updated. Thereafter, as and when there is any change in the above information, same also needs to be updated on the NEAPS portal. The above mentioned details can be updated under the following path: NEAPS > Masters > Paid up Equity capital (Diluted basis). All listed entities are advised to take the necessary steps to be in compliance with the provisions of this Circular. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Manasi Sawant Chief Manager
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has issued Circular No. NSE/CML/2025/09 dated February 28, 2025, requiring all listed companies to ensure that their paid-up equity capital data is updated on the NEAPS portal on both a normal basis and a fully diluted basis, measured in number of shares, together with the applicable conversion ratio details. This circular is issued with reference to SEBI Circular No. IMD/FPIC/CIR/P/2018/61 dated April 5, 2018, which relates to monitoring foreign investment limits in listed Indian companies, and it clarifies that the Exchange has observed many companies have not updated this information on NEAPS.

The compliance action required is twofold: first, every listed company must make a one-time update of its paid-up equity capital and paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis on the NEAPS portal if it has not already done so, even if the company has no outstanding convertible instruments; second, after that initial update, companies must keep the information current and update it whenever there is any change. The prescribed portal path for the update is NEAPS > Masters > Paid up Equity capital (Diluted basis).

No separate compliance deadline is stated in the circular, but the instruction is immediate and ongoing, and listed entities are advised to take necessary steps to comply with the circular’s requirements. The affected entities are all listed companies / listed entities on the NSE, and the obligation specifically concerns the reporting of paid-up equity capital figures on a fully diluted basis for foreign investment limit monitoring purposes.

The circular updates the existing “single filing system” for stock exchange reporting by extending API-based integrated filing to **Integrated Filing (Governance)**, effective **March 1, 2025**, under **NSE/CML/2025/07 dated February 28, 2025**. It is addressed to **all listed entities** and builds on the earlier circular **NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**. From the effective date, the single-filing/API integration is available for governance-related disclosures tied to **SEBI LODR Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30**, meaning companies covered by those reporting obligations should use the integrated filing channel rather than submitting duplicate filings to both exchanges.

The circular clarifies the rollout status for several disclosure categories. **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** was effective **October 1, 2024** and is now **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to the **SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**. **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** became effective **October 26, 2024**; **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** became effective **November 15, 2024**; and **Meetings of shareholders and voting under Regulation 44(3)** became effective **December 28, 2024**. The table indicates applicability by issuer type: the **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** and **Meetings of shareholders and voting** are marked for **equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies, while **exclusively debt** and **REITs/INVITs** are shown as not applicable for those rows; for **Corporate Governance Report** and the integrated governance filing row, the table states that applicability for some categories will be **“communicated later.”**

From a compliance perspective, the key operational instruction is that listed entities should **avoid multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges** now that the aim is a true single-filing system. If, after submission, **one Exchange requests clarification**, the company must respond **to that specific Exchange that raised the query**, rather than replying generically or only through the other exchange. For implementation support, the circular directs companies to contact the relevant team through **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**.

The key compliance implication is for **all listed entities that enter into RPTs requiring audit committee approval and, where thresholds/applicable rules require, shareholder approval**. The document does not itself set out any numerical thresholds or monetary limits in the excerpt provided, but it clearly reinforces that the required approval process under the LODR Regulations must be supported by the prescribed minimum information package. Compliance officers should treat this as an immediate governance/documentation update affecting board/audit committee materials, shareholder meeting notes or explanatory statements, and internal controls over RPT approvals.

No separate implementation date or transition period is stated in the text you provided beyond the circular date itself, so the safe reading is that the industry standards apply from the date of the SEBI circular, **February 14, 2025**, subject to the detailed contents of the enclosed industry standards note. rows.title: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2025/04 Date: February 07, 2025 To All Listed Entities, Subject: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 This is with reference to the recent amendment made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India to regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 vide notification dated December 12, 2024. It is clarified that listed entities shall ensure a minimum gap of at least three working days between the date of board/shareholders’ approval, as applicable to the specific corporate action mentioned in Regulation 42 (1), and the Record Date fixed for such purpose. The minimum gap shall be exclusive of the date of board/shareholder's approval and the actual record date. Further, as per latest amendment, sub-regulation 5 of Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 has been omitted. Hence the listed entities are not required to announce dates of closure of their transfer books for any purpose. All Listed entities are requested to take note of the same and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Senior Manager Harshad Dharod
rows.summary:
This circular clarifies how listed entities must fix the **record date** under **Regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015** following SEBI’s amendment notified on **December 12, 2024**. From this clarification, a listed entity must ensure a **minimum gap of at least three working days** between the **date of board approval or shareholders’ approval** (depending on what is applicable for the relevant corporate action under Regulation 42(1)) and the **record date** set for that corporate action. The three-working-day gap must be calculated **excluding both the approval date and the actual record date**, so the intervening working days are what matter.

The circular also notes a separate compliance change: **Regulation 42(5) has been omitted**. As a result, listed entities are **no longer required to announce closure dates of transfer books for any purpose**. This applies to **all listed entities** and to any corporate action covered by **Regulation 42(1)**. The circular is dated **February 07, 2025**, and the exchange instructs listed entities to take note and **comply accordingly**.

rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange implements SEBI’s December 31, 2024 circular and the related amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, which were published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024. Its main effect is to introduce “Integrated Filing” for listed entities, with separate PDF submissions for governance and financial disclosures using the SEBI-prescribed format, while the existing XBRL/PDF filings for the underlying compliances must continue until further notice. The new regime applies to filings for the quarter ending December 31, 2024 and thereafter.

For timing, the first quarterly Integrated Filing for the December 31, 2024 quarter may be submitted within 45 days from quarter-end, but after that the deadlines split: Integrated Filing (Governance) is due within 30 days from the end of each quarter, while Integrated Filing (Financial) is due within 45 days from the end of each quarter other than the last quarter, and within 60 days from the end of the last quarter of the financial year. The circular also clarifies that, for the December 2024 quarter, the “governance” and “financial” integrated filings are both covered by that one-time 45-day filing window. The listed entity must submit the integrated filing in PDF on the NSE platform using the new announcement subjects “Integrated Filing- Governance” and “Integrated Filing- Financial,” located under Type of Disclosure: “Others” and Subject Category: “Integrated Filing” at NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Action > Create Announcement.

The circular also imposes a specific data-protection requirement: PAN details must be masked in the PDF submissions. In addition, the Exchange states that existing filing obligations remain in place for the underlying items, including corporate governance and investor grievance-related XBRL filings, Regulation 30 event disclosures in PDF/XBRL as applicable, financial results filings, impact of audit qualification (annual), statement of deviations or utilization of funds (SOD), related party transactions (RPT) half-yearly filing, quarterly disclosure of outstanding defaults on loans/debt securities, and board-meeting outcome filings for financials under the current process and timelines. For the December 2024 quarter, the examples given indicate that financial outcome filings and some Regulation 30 event filings continue under their current timelines, while the integrated PDF itself must be filed according to the new schedule. The circular instructs listed entities to comply immediately with these requirements and directs queries to the NSE Listing Compliance team through NEAPS or takeover@nse.co.in.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/36 on November 14, 2024, updating its earlier circular NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024 on the “single filing system” enabled through API-based integration between stock exchanges. The key change is that, effective November 15, 2024, the single-filing mechanism is extended to filings of the **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** of the SEBI (LODR) framework / depository regulations. This means listed entities can now submit this disclosure once through the integrated system rather than separately filing the same disclosure on both exchanges.

The circular specifies that, with this extension, the single filing system is available for the following disclosures and entity categories: **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** for **equity listed companies** and **equity + debt listed companies** (while for **exclusively debt-listed companies** and **REITs/InvITs**, this will be communicated later); **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** for **equity**, **equity + debt**, and **exclusively debt** listed companies (with REITs/InvITs to be communicated later); and now **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** for **equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies only, not for exclusively debt-listed companies or REITs/InvITs. The circular does not change the underlying filing obligation itself, but changes the filing method by centralizing the submission through the API-based single filing system.

For compliance purposes, NSE explicitly instructs listed entities to **avoid multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges**, since the objective is a true single-filing process. If one exchange requests clarification after submission, the company must respond to **the same exchange that raised the query**, rather than duplicating responses elsewhere. Any questions on the circular are to be directed through the NEAPS platform path **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or by email to **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange’s circular dated **November 13, 2024 (NSE/CML/2024/35)** reiterates and expands the compliance expectations around the **Structured Digital Database (SDD)** under **Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015**. It states that these PIT provisions apply not only to listed entities, but also to **unlisted companies that are being listed pursuant to a scheme approved by the NCLT**.

For such companies, the key new requirement is that they must **submit an SDD Certificate from a Practicing Company Secretary (PCS)** **at the time of filing the listing application with the stock exchanges**, certifying that the company is compliant with **Regulations 3(5) and 3(6)** of the SEBI PIT Regulations, including any future amendments. This is a filing-time obligation, so compliance must be established before the application is submitted; it is not enough to remedy deficiencies later.

The circular also says it is **effective immediately**, meaning listed entities and any NCLT-scheme-based applicants should treat the requirement as in force from **November 13, 2024** onward. The Exchange references its earlier circular **NSE/CML/2024/31 dated October 18, 2024**, indicating this communication is a continuation of that prior guidance.

For compliance teams, the practical implication is that any affected entity should ensure its insider-trading controls and SDD records are fully operational, documented, and PCS-verifiable before filing, because the Exchange expects certification of compliance as part of the listing process. All listed companies are instructed to **take note and comply accordingly**.

rows.title: Circular for fetching of documents from Tax Service Platform available with Depository by Listed Companies for giving tax claim relief to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from the perspective of ease of doing business
rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/32 Date: October 25, 2024 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Fetching of document from Tax Service Platform available with Depository by Listed Companies for giving tax claim relief to Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPls) from the perspective of ease of doing business. Dear Sir/ Madam, Pursuant to the amendments made in the Income Tax Act by the Finance Acts, 2020, 2021 and 2023, dividend and interest paid by companies are taxable in the hands of shareholders and bond holders. Further, the companies are required to deduct tax at source (TDS) at the rates applicable to each category of the shareholder. However, certain categories of domestic Investors are exempted while for other categories like Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPIs), tax has to be deducted at 20% (plus surcharge and cess) or at a beneficial tax rate applicable under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). In case of FPIs, Custodians/FPIs are required to provide certain set of documents like Form 10F, permanent establishment document, tax residency certificate to every company which is declaring dividend/interest to claim tax benefit. With a view to manage the operational challenges of providing same set of client documents/details to every company, NSDL has developed a tax services platform to enable Custodians to upload such client documents once in a financial year which can be accessed by Issuers and Registrars and Transfer Agent (RTAs) for determining the rate for tax deductions. From an ease of doing business perspective, all the Listed Companies are requested to take note of the aforesaid Tax Service Platform for fetching required documents for giving tax claim benefit in respect of tax withheld at source in case of dividend/interest income for FPIs. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Ajit Mahadik Manager – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This circular asks all listed entities to use NSDL’s Tax Service Platform, accessed through the depository, to fetch FPI tax-relief documents for dividend and interest payments instead of repeatedly collecting the same paperwork from custodians/FPIs. It is issued by NSE Listing Compliance (Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/32) on October 25, 2024, and is framed as an “ease of doing business” measure rather than a change to the underlying tax law.

The circular explains the legal context: under amendments made by the Finance Acts of 2020, 2021, and 2023, dividends and interest paid by companies are taxable in the hands of shareholders/bondholders, and companies must deduct tax at source (TDS) at the rate applicable to each investor category. For FPIs, the standard withholding rate is 20% plus surcharge and cess, unless a lower treaty rate is available under the relevant Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). Domestic investors may be exempt in certain cases, but the operational focus of this circular is on FPIs receiving dividend or interest income.

The key operational change is that custodians/FPIs can upload the required client documents once in a financial year to NSDL’s tax services platform, and issuers/companies and RTAs can then access those documents directly to determine the correct withholding rate. The documents specifically mentioned are Form 10F, the permanent establishment declaration/document, and the tax residency certificate. The stated purpose is to reduce the burden of submitting the same set of documents to each individual company making a dividend or interest payment.

For compliance teams at listed companies, the practical requirement is to note and use this platform when determining whether an FPI qualifies for treaty relief or any other reduced tax rate, rather than relying solely on direct collection from the investor each time. The circular does not set a new deadline or mandate a new statutory filing, but it does encourage adoption of this centralized document-fetching mechanism for withholding-tax compliance on FPI dividend and interest payments.

rows.title: Introduction of the single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/28 Date: September 30, 2024 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Introduction of the single filing system through API-based integration between Stock Exchanges This is in reference to the SEBI’s consultation paper dated June 26, 2024, titled ‘Recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business and harmonization of the provisions of ICDR and LODR regulations.’ The Committee had recommended that filing done on one Stock Exchange should be automatically disseminated to other Stock Exchange. Both the Exchanges had jointly initiated the development for the API integration to facilitate the same. In this connection, the first phase for the single filing system shall be implemented for “equity” listed and “equity and debt” listed companies for disclosure of Grievance Redressal Mechanism falling under Regulation 13(3) of SEBI LODR from October 01, 2024, onwards, which will be effective for the disclosures to be filed for quarter ended September 30, 2024. Once the aforesaid disclosure is filed on one Exchange it should be ensured that the acknowledgment is received from both the Exchanges. However, post filing as a measure of abundant precaution the listed entities have to check that the filings are available on both the Exchanges websites. The listed entities will have an option for filing the aforesaid disclosure and revision in filings at any one Exchange.
